Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to
on the agenda are on file in the office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection. If
applicable, materials related to an item on this agenda submitted to the Council after distribution of the
agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk’s office during normal business
hours. Any person having any question concerning any agenda item may call the City Clerk to make
inquiry concerning the item. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be
made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the
Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours
prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings; however,
to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make a
presentation shall be limited to three (3) minutes. Anyone wishing to address the City Council must
fill out a green speaker’s card available at the end of each row in the Chambers. The card permits
the City to identify persons for purposes of City Council minute preparation. Please see specific
agenda sections below for any other requirements related to meeting participation. The City
Council, at the direction of the Mayor with concurrence of the Council, may modify the order of
items shown on the agenda.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

PROTEST HEARINGS OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALOS VERDES
ESTATES DECLARING THAT WEEDS GROWING UPON OR IN FRONT OF, AND
BRUSH, RUBBISH, REFUSE, AND DIRT UPON AND IN FRONT OF CERTAIN
IMPROVED AND UNIMPROVED PRIVATE PROPERTIES IN THE CITY ARE A
PUBLIC NUISANCE, AND DECLARING ITS INTENTION TO PROVIDE FOR THE
ABATEMENT THEREOF

City Manager Hoefgen reported that on February 9th Council adopted Resolutions setting this
meeting as the Public Hearing for the County Agricultural Commissioner’s Office weed abatement
program (unimproved parcels) County and Fire Department process (improved parcels). All
property owners listed in the Resolution have received notice of the need to clean and make
improvements on their properties dealing with potentially hazardous conditions. There are 158
unimproved properties that received notice. There are 465 improved properties that received notice.
The County departments incur all the costs related to the clean-up which are then passed on to the
property owner if they choose not take action to complete the clean-up. The clean-up must be
completed before June 2010.

Councilmember Goodhart believed there will be a substantial fire season this year and asked the
Fire Department representatives about the possibility of the Fire Department rating homes on brush
fire survivability.

Robert Walton of LAC Fire Brush Clearance Section said the risk conditions are noted and taken
into consideration when the inspections are made for corrections.

Councilmember Goodhart would like potentially “at risk” properties on the edge of canyons to be
forewarned by the City or the County.

CITY COUNCIL  2
 Chief Barry Nugent said fire personnel do look at the surrounding conditions during inspections and
take them into consideration when they make recommendations to the homeowners to help prevent
fires that start in a brush area from escalating (to a home).

Councilmember Goodhart would like to make sure the property owners are informed of their risk.

Chief Nugent said he will make sure that the homeowners are informed of any potential fire dangers
as part of issuing the clearance notices.

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing and seeing no one wishing to speak, closed the public
hearing.

It was moved by Councilmember Goodhart, seconded by Councilmember Bird, and unanimously
approved to adopt a minute resolution directing the County Agricultural Commissioner’s Office
(CACO) to inspect and abate weeds, brush, rubbish, and refuse as necessary on unimproved lots
contained in the adjusted list and to direct the Los Angeles County Fire Department to inspect all
improved properties before affirmation of the final list.

ORDINANCE

INTRODUCTION OF ORDINANCE 10-696; AMENDING CHAPTER 9 OF THE PALOS
VERDES ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO PICKETING

Chief Dreiling reported that on several occasions each year the police department is called upon to
protect the homes of some residents from unwanted picketers. PVE’s current Municipal Code is
overly broad and unenforceable. The picketing demonstrators push their disruptive conduct to the
limit of the laws and the demonstrations can last for many hours including after dark. Chief
Dreiling and City Attorney Pannone developed the proposed amendment to the Municipal Code
taking into account what has worked in other jurisdictions. The new ordinance would prohibit
targeted picketing: 1) within two hundred (200) feet from the property line upon which the targeted
residential dwelling is located, 2) except during daylight hours, and, 3) for more than one hour
during any twenty-four (24) hour period. Additionally, the ordinance includes a prohibition against
“dangerous sticks and poles.”

There was Council discussion on the proper distance that picketers should be restricted from the
property line of the targeted home which would provide the proper space required to allow the
Police Officers to do their job safely and also preserve the tranquility of the neighborhood.

It was moved by Mayor Pro Tem Humphrey, seconded by Councilmember Rea, and unanimously
approved, by a roll call vote, to introduce Ordinance 10-696; titled “An Ordinance of the City
Council of the City of Palos Verdes Estates Amending Chapter 9.05 of the Palos Verdes Estates
Municipal Code Relating to Picketing.”

It was moved by Councilmember Rea and seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Humphrey that the
demands, as approved by a majority of the City Council No. 516992 to 517060 totaling $836,535.20
be allowed and it was unanimously approved.

CITY COUNCIL  3
 MAYOR & CITY COUNCILMEMBERS’ REPORTS

Mayor Perkins reported that the sewage spill in Lunada Bay a few weeks ago (County Sanitation
District broken sewer line) was contained within one hour of the spill being reported.

Mayor Perkins reporting on the County Sanitation District Board Meeting, said that the Marine Life
Protection Act, that has a proposed preservation area near Pt. Vicente, may create new clean water
regulations could cause the Sanitation District to be fined due to one of their outfalls being adjacent to
the preservation area. As a result, the Sanitation District intends to oppose the inclusion of this location
as a protected area.

Mayor Perkins attended a reception for Congresswoman Jane Harman and Congressman Peter Defazio
regarding transportation issues. They are trying to accelerate federal funding for some South Bay
transportation projects.

Mayor Pro Tem Humphrey announced that Judy Mitchell, Councilmember from RHE, was elected as
the AQMD representative for South Bay Cities.

Mayor Pro Tem Humphrey reported that she, the City Manager, and Councilmember Goodhart attend
the PV Transit Budget Workshop on February 18th. She also attended the Chamber of Commerce’s
“Salute to Business” where Malaga Bank was recognized as “Best Business 2010.”

Councilmember Rea reported that the CJPIA may be moving from a rolling retrospective formula to a
prospective formula.

Councilmember Goodhart attended the Metropolitan Transportation Authority quarterly meeting of the
Service Sector Councils. The MTA is facing a $100 million to $150 million deficit and they are
reorganizing.

Councilmember Bird announced that CERT training will be held in March for anyone interested.

ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business before Council the meeting was adjourned at 8:40 p.m. to Tuesday,
March 9, 2010 at 7:30 p.m. in the City Council Chambers of City Hall.
